weather.tip: Mostly clear and mild at 21.5°C right now, but a 47% rain chance later means a stray shower is a real possibility — carry a light rain jacket and build in extra time if your commute runs through the newly restricted flyovers.

around.headline: Traffic police book 690+ drunk-driving and over-speeding cases in a week as two more die in road accidents
around.summary: Bengaluru Traffic Police registered over 690 drunk-driving and over-speeding cases in the past week, per The Hindu, even as two people were killed and three injured in separate road accidents in the city and four died in a Bengaluru-Chennai Expressway crash while returning from Tirupati, per The Indian Express. If you're driving back late from a long weekend trip, budget for fatigue stops and expect checkpoints on the way in.

around.headline: New flyover restrictions on goods vehicles are adding to traffic chaos
around.summary: Following over 3,300 breakdowns across three flyovers in 19 months, authorities have restricted goods vehicles on affected stretches, and commuters report journeys taking twice as long since the curbs kicked in, per The Hindu and Deccan Herald. Check which flyovers near your route are affected before you plan a trip that would normally cut through one.

around.headline: Metro's Pink Line inches toward a September launch
around.summary: BMRCL has received the rolling-stock nod needed to bring the Bannerghatta Road corridor into service, with the Pink Line reportedly ready for a September launch, per Construction World and Deccan Herald. Worth watching if your commute currently detours around that stretch, since a launch could shave real time off it.

around.headline: SIR voter-roll hearings descend into chaos as 83% of Karnataka notices remain undelivered
around.summary: Day 1 of Special Intensive Revision (SIR) hearings in Bengaluru saw confusion, with elderly residents especially left unclear on the process, while 83% of SIR notices across Karnataka are yet to reach voters and citizens abroad are seeking easier hearing options, per The Times of India and The Hindu. If you haven't received your SIR notice yet, don't assume you're off the hook — check your status on the Election Commission's portal rather than waiting for paper to arrive.
around.source: The Times of India, The Hindu

around.headline: Karnataka High Court calls the KPSC recruitment scam 'systematic fraud', denies bail to ex-chairman
around.summary: The High Court refused anticipatory bail to the Karnataka Public Service Commission's former chairman, describing the recruitment scam under investigation as 'systematic fraud', per Bar and Bench. A reminder that even official-looking government recruitment processes aren't immune to manipulation — if a 'guaranteed selection' offer for a government job ever comes with a price tag, that's the fraud, not a shortcut.

around.headline: Delhi building collapse death toll rises to 7; HC orders citywide PG inspections
around.summary: The death toll from a Delhi building collapse has climbed to seven, and the High Court has ordered a citywide inspection of paying-guest and student housing, per The Hindu. If you live in a PG or an older rented building in Bengaluru, it's worth asking your landlord or RWA when the structure was last inspected, especially if you've noticed cracks or unauthorised floor additions.

around.headline: Bengaluru ranks 32nd in the Centre's clean-air survey, trailing Mumbai and Hyderabad
around.summary: Bengaluru placed 32nd in the government's latest clean-air city ranking, behind Mumbai and Hyderabad, per The Times of India and India Today. If you exercise outdoors, early morning near arterial roads is still your best bet for cleaner air before traffic builds up.
around.source: The Times of India, India Today

street_smart.title: You've booked an appliance repair technician through a phone number on a sticker, and midway through fixing your fridge in your home, he starts making inappropriate advances — like today's Bengaluru case where a fridge technician molested a woman at her home and was beaten by neighbours before police arrived. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: TOI Bengaluru, Sept 8 — 'Fridge technician molests woman at Bengaluru home, beaten up.' This mechanism (home-service worker safety) hasn't been used as a street-smart scenario in the last three weeks.
street_smart.situation: You're alone at home. The nearest exit is a few steps behind him, and your phone is on the table beside you.

choices.text: Immediately put distance between yourself and him, move toward the door, loudly state you're uncomfortable and want him to leave, then call the police helpline (112) or the women's helpline (1091) right away, keeping his booking ID and phone number for the complaint.
choices.feedback: Correct. Getting to a safe distance and an exit comes before anything else, and a loud, clear statement often stops an opportunistic advance on its own. Calling it in immediately — with his platform booking ID, name, and phone number already in hand from the service app — gives police a verified identity to act on, not just a description.

choices.text: Shout for neighbours and let them confront or beat him before anyone calls the police.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. It's exactly what happened in today's case, and it feels like justice in the moment — but mob violence is itself a criminal offence, it can injure bystanders, and a technician who is beaten first can later claim self-defence or dispute what actually happened, muddying the real case against him. Restraining him calmly until police arrive, or simply letting him go while you call it in, protects your own legal position far better than joining a beating.

choices.text: Ask him to leave quietly and don't file a complaint, reasoning it's over and you'd rather avoid the hassle.
choices.feedback: Risky. Without a report, there's no record tying him to an offence, and he stays free to visit the next home on his route through the same booking platform. Filing even a brief complaint creates a trail that protects the next person.

choices.text: Complain only to the service platform's customer support and skip the police, expecting the company to blacklist him.
choices.feedback: Risky. A platform can suspend an account, but it has no power to investigate or prosecute an offence — only the police can register an FIR and pursue it as a criminal matter. Report to both, but the police complaint is the one that actually holds him accountable.

takeaways: Book home-service technicians only through platforms or brand service centres that show a verified photo ID and booking record, not a number off a sticker or flyer.
If someone crosses a line in your home, prioritize getting to the door over confronting them — you can always call it in once you're safely clear.
Karnataka's police helpline is 112 and the women's helpline is 1091; a formal complaint using the technician's booking ID is what actually gets him barred from future jobs, not silence or a beating.

quiz.question: Why have authorities restricted goods vehicles on several Bengaluru flyovers this week, according to today's reports?
options: Because of over 3,300 breakdowns on three flyovers in 19 months
To make way for Metro construction
quiz.why: Frequent breakdowns, often from overloaded goods vehicles, damage flyover surfaces and cause pile-ups, which is why the curbs target heavy vehicles specifically rather than all traffic.

quiz.question: The chaotic 'SIR' hearings making news in Bengaluru this week refer to a revision of what?
quiz.why: Special Intensive Revision (SIR) is an Election Commission of India exercise to verify and update voter rolls, and its Karnataka round has drawn criticism for reaching only a fraction of voters so far.

quiz.question: The Delhi High Court's citywide inspection order this week, following a building collapse, specifically targets what kind of housing?
quiz.why: The collapse raised concerns specifically about unregulated PG accommodation, which is often converted from residential buildings without the structural checks a purpose-built hostel would require.

quiz.question: Under India's Constitution, what is the minimum age required to contest a Lok Sabha (lower house) election?
quiz.why: The minimum age is 25 for the Lok Sabha but 30 for the Rajya Sabha (upper house), a distinction that trips up many first-time voters.

quiz.question: Which river is the primary source of Bengaluru's piped drinking water, pumped uphill from a reservoir over 100 km away?
quiz.why: Water is drawn from the Cauvery at the Krishna Raja Sagara (KRS) reservoir and pumped uphill in stages to reach the city, which is part of why Bengaluru's water supply is so energy-intensive and vulnerable to drought years.
